hero.name: Tervain · The Wanderer
hero.description: A weathered man in his late thirties who has lost his memory. Low, rough baritone with a little gravel; quiet, restrained and wary, with a dry sense of humour. Speaks plainly and briefly. Neutral northern English accent. Close, intimate recording.
hero.designSample: Salt in my mouth, sand in everything, and no name to go with any of it. Fine. Start with the road, and see who is waiting at the end of it.

caravan_master.name: Tervain · Joss Merrin
caravan_master.description: A caravan master around sixty. Warm, gravelly baritone; unhurried, kindly but tired. Rural northern English accent. A man who has driven wagons all his life.
caravan_master.designSample: Rillford is as far as the wagon goes. The ford road washed out in the thaw, and that bell has been ringing since dawn. Walk inland, friend.

rillford_reeve.name: Tervain · Mara Venn
rillford_reeve.description: A woman around forty, the elected reeve of a farming village. Firm and practical, clear mid-low voice, tired but resolute, warm underneath. West Country English accent.
rillford_reeve.designSample: I am Mara Venn. Rillford elected me to keep it fed, and this morning I have very little to feed anyone with. Look at the channel, then tell me what you see.

spring_steward.name: Tervain · Sister Edda Sorn
spring_steward.description: An elderly woman in her seventies, the devout keeper of a holy spring. Calm, measured and soft, slightly husky, never hurried. Gentle Scottish accent. Serene.
spring_steward.designSample: The spring gives what it is given. Silt, sorrow, patience. Kneel if you wish, stranger, but do not drink until I say the water is clear.

quarry_foreman.name: Tervain · Darin Kest
quarry_foreman.description: A big, gruff quarry foreman in his fifties. Deep, loud, gravelly baritone; blunt and impatient. Broad Yorkshire accent. Used to shouting over stone saws.
quarry_foreman.designSample: The contract says forty blocks by the new moon. The contract doesn't care about the weather, and neither do I. You want work? Then lift something.

maintenance_worker.name: Tervain · Ila Rusk
maintenance_worker.description: A young woman in her mid twenties, a wiry seasonal stoneworker from the cold north. Quick and dry, slightly hoarse voice. Light Scandinavian-tinged English accent. Wary but brave.
maintenance_worker.designSample: Don't look down, they said. Easy for them. The ledge is crumbling, the path is gone, and I have been counting the same three handholds since noon.

estate_steward.name: Tervain · Oren Halvek
estate_steward.description: A thin, well-dressed estate steward in his sixties. Refined, precise, clipped dry tenor. Received pronunciation, faintly condescending, smooth and careful with numbers.
estate_steward.designSample: The delivery date has not moved, and the estate does not move dates. Water is a regrettable problem. Late stone is an expensive one.

ash_recorder.name: Tervain · Sel Anrit
ash_recorder.description: A quiet scholar who keeps records for an order of witnesses. A soft, mid-pitched androgynous voice that could belong to a woman or a man; careful diction, solemn and attentive, a faint Irish lilt. Speaks as if dictating into a ledger.
ash_recorder.designSample: Write it down. Someone must. The day, the weather, who spoke first and who stayed silent. Memory lies. Ink only fades.

shrine_warden.name: Tervain · Tolan Harrow
shrine_warden.description: A stern old knight in his sixties who guards a shrine archive. Deep, authoritative bass-baritone; terse and formal. A slight Welsh accent. Suspicious of strangers, a voice used to giving orders.
shrine_warden.designSample: Keep the lamp out of the archive. Keep your hands where I can see them. The order allows pilgrims at the spring, not thieves at the door.

mill_hand.name: Tervain · Bess Corran
mill_hand.description: A cheerful, earthy woman in her early thirties who works at a water mill. Bright mid voice, plain-spoken, a laugh close to the surface even when worried. East Anglian English accent.
mill_hand.designSample: The wheel hasn't turned since the flood, so here I stand, watching a dry ditch like it owes me money. Go on, ask me how the grain is doing.

quarry_hand.name: Tervain · Pell Dunmore
quarry_hand.description: A tired quarry labourer around forty. Rough, husky tenor; weary and a little mumbling, with dry gallows humour. Working-class Midlands English accent.
quarry_hand.designSample: Nothing to cut with, nothing to drink. Night shift again, they say. Night shift of what? Staring at rocks in the dark?

village_baker.name: Tervain · Hesper Lowe
village_baker.description: A warm, chatty village baker in her fifties. Round, motherly voice, quick and kind, slightly out of breath from work. Cornish English accent.
village_baker.designSample: No water, no dough, my love. I have been baking with the last of the rain barrel and praying over every loaf. Take one. You look like you need it.

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: You came in along the shore road and over the overlook, so you heard the bell. It has not rung in my term until today. I am Mara Venn; Rillford elected me to keep it fed, and this morning I have very little to feed anyone with.
lines.transcript: You came in along the shore road and over the overlook, so you heard the bell. It has not rung in my term until today. I am Mara Venn. Rilford elected me to keep it fed, and this morning I have very little to feed anyone with.

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: The late thaw broke the old sluice upstream and choked the spring channels with silt. The household channel behind the mill is dry — go and see it. The quarry wants water, the shrine wants its share, and I cannot give all three what each is owed.
lines.transcript: The late thaw broke the old sluice upstream and choked the spring channels with silt. The household channel behind the mill is dry. Go and see it. The quarry wants water, the shrine wants its share, and I cannot give all three what each is owed

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: North along the mill lane to the sluice; past it, up the steps, is the spring shrine. The cut track east of the fields leads to the quarry — Darin Kest and his crew. The ford is south-east. The side path off the ford has not been safe lately.
lines.transcript: North along the mill lane to the sluice. Past it, up the steps, is the spring shrine. The cut track east of the fields leads to the quarry, Darren Kest and his crew. The ford is southeast. The side path off the ford has not been safe lately

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: The Hearth League does not turn away hands. Look at the channel, then talk to Darin and to Sister Edda before you decide anything. I would rather you heard all of us than only me.
lines.transcript: The Hearth League does not turn away hands. Look at the channel, then talk to Daryn and to Sister Edda before you decide anything. I would rather you heard all of us than only me

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: What do you need to know?
lines.transcript: What do you need to know?

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: Every household is down to a bucket a day. The communal mill is idle, and without it the planting will not be ground into bread. I promised more relief than the remaining flow can carry — I said days. That is on me. If it comes to one or the other, I would choose the village, and I will not pretend otherwise.
lines.transcript: Every household is down to a bucket a day. The communal mill is idle, and without it, the planting will not be ground into bread. I promised more relief than the remaining flow can carry. I said days. That is on me. If it comes to one or the other, I would choose the village, and I will not pretend otherwise

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: Yes. When the channel first ran short I opened a small side gate above the fields, and I did not call the witnesses the Accord asks for. I told myself it was too small to matter. It is not nothing.
lines.transcript: Yes. When the channel first ran short, I opened a small side gate above the fields, and I did not call the witnesses the Accord asks for. I told myself it was too small to matter. It is not nothing

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: A schedule the whole valley can watch, kept by witnesses. The households have given more labor than the public ledger records — the schedule has to count it. If Darin will sign and Edda will stand as waterkeeper, I will stand for Rillford.
lines.transcript: A schedule the whole valley can watch, kept by witnesses. The households have given more labor than the public ledger records. The schedule has to count it. If Darring will sign and Edda will stand as Water Keeper, I will stand for Rilford

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: So there is a record. Then we can say plainly what the village gave, and ask the quarry for the same honesty. Thank you — it is more than the Templars ever offered me.
lines.transcript: So there is a record. Then we can say plainly what the village gave and ask the quarry for the same honesty. Thank you. It is more than the Templars ever offered me

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: You want the account to say only that the flood broke the sluice? That is not the whole truth, and you know it. But it would spare people. …I do not like it. I will not contradict you.
lines.transcript: You want the account to say only that the flood broke the sluice? That is not the whole truth, and you know it. But it would spare people. I do not like it. I will not contradict you

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: Someone forced the sluice, and the household channel is worse than yesterday. Whoever it was, the gate is jammed now. It will need a proper brace and a hand that knows what it is doing before anyone gets a drop.
lines.transcript: Someone forced the sluice and the household channel is worse than yesterday. Whoever it was, the gate is jammed now. It will need a proper brace and a hand that knows what it is doing before anyone gets a drop

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: The channel behind the mill is filling — I can hear it. The wheel will turn by midday. It cost the quarry, and I know it. This is an emergency allocation; the Accord says it expires unless reviewed. We will owe a review.
lines.transcript: The channel behind the mill is filling. I can hear it. The wheel will turn by midday. It costs the quarry, and I know it. This is an emergency allocation. The accord says it expires unless reviewed. We will owe a review

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: The mill sits still and the households still ration. I said I would abide by what you decided, and I will — but Rillford is protesting, and so am I. An emergency allocation expires unless it is reviewed.
lines.transcript: The mill sits still and the households still ration. I said I would abide by what you decided, and I will. But Rilford is protesting, and so am I. An emergency allocation expires unless it is reviewed

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: There it is on the board: mill by day, quarry by night. Neither of us has what we asked for. It will hold as long as we keep watching it — and we will. Witnessed, as the Accord asks.
lines.transcript: There it is on the board. Mill by day, quarry by night. Neither of us has what we asked for. It will hold as long as we keep watching it, and we will. Witnessed, as the accord asks

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: Water in the channel. Bread by the weekend. Darin's crew will not forgive it soon; I have asked Bess to take the idle crew's hours against our stores as far as we can stretch. Rillford owes you, and I will not forget which side of it we were on.
lines.transcript: Water in the channel. Bread by the weekend. Darren's crew will not forgive it soon. I have asked Bess to take the idle crew's hours against our stores as far as we can stretch. Rilford owes you, and I will not forget which side of it we were on

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: The quarry cuts again, the delivery goes out, and my neighbors queue at the well. I can carry that a season. Not two. I will bring it to review, and I will bring the ledger with me.
lines.transcript: The quarry cuts again, the delivery goes out, and my neighbors queue at the well. I can carry that a season, not two. I will bring it to review, and I will bring the ledger with me

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: Half a mill and half a quarry, and both of them angry with me for promising less than they wanted. That is what a fair schedule looks like. Come and see the night crew in the morning; they will tell you what it costs.
lines.transcript: Half a mill and half a quarry, and both of them angry with me for promising less than they wanted. That is what a fair schedule looks like. Come and see the night crew in the morning. They will tell you what it costs

lines.speaker: rillford_reeve
lines.text: A witnessed rotation, with the waterkeeper standing for it, is the kind of change the Accord recognizes. An emergency allocation is not — it lapses unless reviewed, and nobody owns the water for having held the gate. Whichever you chose, that is the truth of it.
lines.transcript: A witnessed rotation, with the Waterkeeper standing for it, is the kind of change the Accord recognizes. An emergency allocation is not. It lapses unless reviewed, and nobody owns the water for having held the gate. Whichever you chose, that is the truth of it.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: You have the look of someone walking since dawn. I am Sister Edda Sorn, waterkeeper of this spring. If Rillford has sent you, tell them the spring still gives what it can — it is the channels below that have failed, not the water at its source.
lines.transcript: You have the look of someone walking since dawn. I am Sister Edda Sorn, Water Keeper of this spring. If Rilford has sent you, tell them the spring still gives what it can. It is the channels below that have failed, not the water at its source.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The flood laid silt through the intake channels. The flow is thin, but the wetland lives. Go and look at the intake yourself before you listen to anyone who says the spring is failing.
lines.transcript: The flood laid silt through the intake channels. The flow is thin, but the wetland lives. Go and look at the intake yourself before you listen to anyone who says the spring is failing

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The spring is quiet today. What would you ask?
lines.transcript: The spring is quiet today. What would you ask?

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The foreman says the spring is failing. It is not failing — sediment obstructs it. If you doubt me, kneel at the intake and put your hand in.
lines.transcript: The foreman says the spring is failing. It is not failing. Sediment obstructs it. If you doubt me, kneel at the intake and put your hand in.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The support beside the gate cracked in the flood. I have not examined it closely since. An inspection was due before the thaw, and the roads were closed. I would not force that gate open — it could give way.
lines.transcript: The support beside the gate cracked in the flood. I have not examined it closely since. An inspection was due before the thaw and the roads were closed. I would not force that gate open. It could give way.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: …Yes. I deferred it. I told myself the roads were closed; the truth is I trusted old stone. I will say so publicly if it helps. The order preaches restraint, and I let restraint become neglect.
lines.transcript: Yes, I deferred it. I told myself the roads were closed. The truth is, I trusted Old Stone. I will say so publicly if it helps. The Order preaches restraint, and I let restraint become neglect.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: You have seen what the flood left at the intake, so you have a reason. The archive is not a public room. Warden Harrow keeps the door; tell him I said yes. Read what you need, and put it back where you found it.
lines.transcript: You have seen what the flood left at the intake, so you have a reason. The archive is not a public room. Warden Harrow keeps the door. Tell him I said yes. Read what you need and put it back where you found it.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The rite calms an unstable flow for a while — perhaps forty minutes — long enough to work the sluice safely. It does not make water; it makes a gate less violent. It takes a votive reed, and I have one to spare. There is no second.
lines.transcript: The rite calms an unstable flow for a while, perhaps forty minutes, long enough to work the sluice safely. It does not make water; it makes a gate less violent. It takes a votive reed, and I have one to spare. There is no second.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The minimum flow to the wetland stays as the Accord sets it. The sluice is braced before anything is opened. Both users' needs are written down and witnessed. If all that is done, yes — I will stand for the spring.
lines.transcript: The minimum flow to the wetland stays as the accord sets it. The sluice is braced before anything is opened. Both users' needs are written down and witnessed. If all that is done, yes, I will stand for the spring

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: I know about the archive shutter. I will not pretend otherwise. Access is withdrawn; the key stays with Harrow. Trust is a thing I give slowly, and you have spent some of it.
lines.transcript: I know about the archive shutter. I will not pretend otherwise. Access is withdrawn. The key stays with Harrow. Trust is a thing I give slowly, and you have spent some of it

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: Someone forced the gate. I warned you it could give way. It has, in the quietest way it could — jammed rather than broken. Brace it properly, and this can still be mended.
lines.transcript: Someone forced the gate. I warned you it could give way. It has, in the quietest way it could, jammed rather than broken. Brace it properly and this can still be mended

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The wetland has its minimum, and the village has its water. It is an emergency allocation, and it lapses unless it is reviewed — I will hold the review, and the quarry will be there.
lines.transcript: The wetland has its minimum and the village has its water. It is an emergency allocation and it lapses unless it is reviewed. I will hold the review and the quarry will be there.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: The wetland has its minimum; the rest goes to stone. It is an emergency allocation, and I will remind the reeve and the estate that it lapses unless it is reviewed. The spring has borne worse.
lines.transcript: The wetland has its minimum. The rest goes to Stone. It is an emergency allocation, and I will remind the Reeve and the estate that it lapses unless it is reviewed. The spring has borne worse.

lines.speaker: spring_steward
lines.text: A schedule witnessed by the reeve, the foreman and the spring. This is what the Accord meant. Keep the sluice braced and the log current — I will not miss another inspection.
lines.transcript: A schedule witnessed by the reeve, the foreman, and the spring. This is what the accord meant. Keep the sluice braced and the log current. I will not miss another inspection.

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: Quarry is stopped for the day: no water to cut with, less to drink. Darin Kest. If the reeve sent you to tell me to shut down, save your breath. I have a Marcher contract and a delivery that will not wait on the weather.
lines.transcript: Quarry is stopped for the day. No water to cut with, less to drink. Darren Kest. If the Reeve sent you to tell me to shut down, save your breath. I have a Marcher contract and a delivery that will not wait on the weather

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: The spring is failing, that is what. Flow off the mountain is down to a trickle and Rillford has siphoned what is left. I told Sister Edda; she told me to wait for the Templars' inspection.
lines.transcript: The spring is failing, that is what. Flow off the mountain is down to a trickle, and Rydford has siphoned what is left. I told Sister Edda. She told me to wait for the Templars' inspection

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: Well?
lines.transcript: Well

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: We cut a short extension after the permission ran out. The seep came in after. I do not know whether it undermined anything. My crew reported it. Nobody came. That is the truth, and I will say it to the steward's face.
lines.transcript: We cut a short extension after the permission ran out. The seep came in after. I do not know whether it undermined anything. My crew reported it. Nobody came. That is the truth, and I will say it to the steward's face.

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: Ila Rusk — Rimeward stoneworker on seasonal maintenance. She went along the cut path to read the seep gully and something big took the path from her. There is an old maintenance gate; its lever is by the lower stack. It opens a way round.
lines.transcript: Isla Rusk, Reamwood stoneworker on seasonal maintenance. She went along the cut path to read the seep gully, and something big took the path from her. There is an old maintenance gate. Its lever is by the lower stack. It opens a way round

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: That brace is Rillford's — on loan since the last repair, not mine to keep. Take it, and the wrench beside it, if you can use them. Fix the gate before anyone else decides to force it.
lines.transcript: That brace is Rilford's, on loan since the last repair. Not mine to keep. Take it and the wrench beside it if you can use them. Fix the gate before anyone else decides to force it

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: The Marcher estate wants its stone and its steward wants excuses. Oren Halvek is in the office by the gate; he will tell you the contract stands whatever the weather does. Ask him about the reserve — I would.
lines.transcript: The Marcher Estate wants its stone, and its steward wants excuses. Orin Halvek is in the office by the gate. He will tell you the contract stands whatever the weather does. Ask him about the reserve. I would

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: You said that in front of my crew. …Fine. Then you have nothing more to say to me until you take it back.
lines.transcript: You said that in front of my crew. Fine. Then you have nothing more to say to me until you take it back

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: You have seen the sluice for yourself, so you know it is not only my cut. Fine. Sit down. Tell me what you are proposing.

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: The ledger says the quarry ran nights when the mill ran days, a generation ago. If it is a rota the crew can read on a board, and the sluice is braced, I will sign it. My crew will grumble about the nights. They always did.

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: Night shifts cost my crew sleep, and I have nothing on paper to show them it has been done before. Put ten coin behind a shift bonus and I will sign, and you will not have to prove anything else.
lines.transcript: Night shifts cost my crew sleep, and I have nothing on paper to show them it has been done before. Put ten coin behind a shift bonus and I will sign, and you will not have to prove anything else

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman
lines.text: Water in the cutting trench again. The delivery can go out. I will not thank you for the village's trouble, but my crew eats.
lines.transcript: Water in the cutting trench again. The delivery can go out. I will not thank you for the village's trouble, but my crew eats

lines.speaker: quarry_foreman

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: You opened the gate! And walked round the ledge without a fight. Clever. Give me a moment — I will meet you in Rillford, and I will tell you what I saw in the gully.

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: You opened the gate! I walked the old track round the ledge and never met the beast. Here is what I saw before it came: fresh fractures on the support beside the gate, silt across the intake, and the seep in the quarry gully feeding the wrong channel. Close the gate slowly, from the downstream side, with the brace set before you turn the wheel. Do it that way and it will not surge.
lines.transcript: You opened the gate! I walked the old track round the ledge and never met the beast. Here is what I saw before it came: fresh fractures on the support beside the gate, silt across the intake, and the seep in the quarry gully feeding the wrong channel. lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: I am not going anywhere until my legs agree. What do you want to know?
lines.transcript: I am not going anywhere until my legs agree. What do you want to know?

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: From the downstream side. Set the brace against the cracked post first, turn the wheel a quarter, wait for the water to settle, then another quarter. If the flow is calm — the rite, if Sister Edda taught you — it will not push back at all.
lines.transcript: From the downstream side. Set the brace against the cracked post first, turn the wheel a quarter, wait for the water to settle, then another quarter. If the flow is calm, the right, if Sister Edda taught you, it will not push back at all.

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: Nobody. That is what frightens me. A late flood on a sluice nobody inspected, a town side-gate nobody witnessed, a quarry cut nobody permitted. Each small. Together, a dry village. Do not look for a villain; look for who will keep the pieces from failing again.
lines.transcript: Nobody. That is what frightens me. A late flood on a sluice nobody inspected. A town side gate nobody witnessed. A quarry cut nobody permitted. Each small. Together, a dry village. Do not look for a villain. Look for who will keep the pieces from failing again

lines.speaker: maintenance_worker
lines.text: I am walking home to the Rimeward Heights when the road allows. Tell the reeve the brace wants checking after the first rain. Whatever you chose, keep the sluice honest.
lines.transcript: I am walking home to the Reamwood Heights when the road allows. Tell the Reeve the brace wants checking after the first rain. Whatever you chose, keep the sluice honest

lines.speaker: estate_steward
lines.text: Steward Halvek, Marcher estate. If you are here about the delivery, the contract stands regardless of who has water. As for the repair reserve — it is sufficient.
lines.transcript: Stuart Halvek, Marcher Estate. If you are here about the delivery, the contract stands regardless of who has water. As for the repair reserve, it is sufficient

lines.speaker: estate_steward
lines.text: …It is empty. The estate has not funded repairs since the winter levy. Please do not repeat it. If you must, say the estate is reviewing its commitments.
lines.transcript: It is empty. The estate has not funded repairs since the winter levy. Please do not repeat it. If you must, say the estate is reviewing its commitments

lines.speaker: estate_steward
lines.text: The contract stands. The delivery date has not moved. Is there something else?
lines.transcript: The contract stands. The delivery date has not moved. Is there something else?

lines.speaker: estate_steward
lines.text: The delivery will go out. The estate notes your part in it. That is not a promise of anything, but it is noted.
lines.transcript: The delivery will go out. The estate notes your part in it. That is not a promise of anything, but it is noted.

lines.speaker: estate_steward
lines.text: The estate is reviewing its commitments. A missed or shared delivery reflects on my ledger, not yours. Good day.
lines.transcript: The estate is reviewing its commitments. A missed or shared delivery reflects on my ledger, not yours. Good day.

lines.speaker: ash_recorder
lines.text: Sel Anrit, recorder. Third failure this season: a bridge, a granary road, now the water. You will call it coincidence. I do not.
lines.transcript: Sel Anrit, recorder. Third failure this season. A bridge, a granary road, now the water. You will call it coincidence. I do not

lines.speaker: ash_recorder
lines.text: I record what others forget. Ask.
lines.transcript: I record what others forget. Ask

lines.speaker: ash_recorder
lines.text: Everything, including an old rotation ledger in the shrine archive. The copies disagree. Ask the steward; the Templars keep it and rarely read it. If you can read it, read it.
lines.transcript: Everything, including an old rotation ledger in the shrine archive. The copies disagree. Ask the steward. The Templars keep it and rarely read it. If you can read it, read it

lines.speaker: ash_recorder
lines.text: Repair only delays it. The pattern is plain: each failure is smaller than the last cause and larger than the last cure. Do not take comfort in patching.
lines.transcript: Repair only delays it. The pattern is plain. Each failure is smaller than the last cause and larger than the last cure. Do not take comfort in patching

lines.speaker: ash_recorder
lines.text: I have written down what you did. I still do not know whether it is a beginning or a delay. But it is written, and that matters.
lines.transcript: I have written down what you did. I still do not know whether it is a beginning or a delay, but it is written, and that matters

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: Warden Tolan Harrow. The archive is locked, and Sister Edda holds the say. If you want steel discipline rather than speeches, I teach a little of it too.
lines.transcript: Warden Tolan Harrow. The archive is locked, and Sister Edda holds the say. If you want steel discipline rather than speeches, I teach a little of it too

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: What do you need?
lines.transcript: What do you need?

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: The Sister's word is enough. The door is open. Do not take anything out, and do not leave the lamp burning.
lines.transcript: The sister's word is enough. The door is open. Do not take anything out and do not leave the lamp burning

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: I should not. But that gate worries me too — it worries all of us. Take the key. Bring it back, and do not let the Sister find that you had it before she agreed.
lines.transcript: I should not. But that gate worries me too. It worries all of us. Take the key, bring it back, and do not let the sister find that you had it before she agreed

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: Steady Guard: raise your guard, blade or bare arms, and it costs you 40% less stamina to hold it, so you can wait out a heavy blow instead of running from it. Ten coin — or nothing, if you have already proved you can stand in front of something dangerous.
lines.transcript: Steady Guard. Raise your guard, blade or bare arms, and it costs you 40% less stamina to hold it, so you can wait out a heavy blow instead of running from it. Ten coin, or nothing if you have already proved you can stand in front of something dangerous

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: Good. Feet apart, guard high, and do not flinch. That is all of it. Come back if you need to remember.
lines.transcript: Good. Feet apart, guard high, and do not flinch. That is all of it. Come back if you need to remember.

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: Anything else?
lines.transcript: Anything else?

lines.speaker: shrine_warden
lines.text: The Sister is gone. I keep the shrine and the noticeboard now. If the valley needs a waterkeeper's witness, I will stand — though it will not carry the weight hers did.
lines.transcript: The Sister is gone. I keep the shrine and the notice board now. If the valley needs a Waterkeeper’s witness, I will stand, though it will not carry the weight hers did.

lines.speaker: mill_hand
lines.text: The wheel has been dry since the flood. Without water I have nothing to grind — I stand here so the reeve sees somebody is minding it.
lines.transcript: The wheel has been dry since the flood. Without water, I have nothing to grind. I stand here so the Reeve sees somebody is minding it

lines.speaker: mill_hand
lines.text: Hear that? The wheel turns! Grain by evening. I will not say what it cost the quarry, but I will say I am glad.
lines.transcript: Hear that? The wheel turns. Grain by evening. I will not say what it cost the quarry, but I will say I am glad

lines.speaker: mill_hand
lines.text: The wheel is dry and the quarry dust is flying. I am not the only one who wanted it the other way.
lines.transcript: The wheel is dry and the quarry dust is flying. I am not the only one who wanted it the other way.

lines.speaker: mill_hand
lines.text: Days for the mill. I mind the board. It is not much, but it is not nothing — and it is written where everyone can read it.
lines.transcript: Days for the mill. I mind the board it is not much, but it is not nothing and it is written where everyone can read it

lines.speaker: quarry_hand
lines.text: Foreman says we wait. Nothing to cut with, nothing to drink. If you are looking for Ila — the Cut path is closed. Something big took the ledge. Foreman knows about the gate.
lines.transcript: Foreman says we wait. Nothing to cut with, nothing to drink. If you are looking for Isla, the cut path is closed. Something big took the ledge. Foreman knows about the gate

lines.speaker: quarry_hand
lines.text: No water, no work, no pay. Rillford got its mill; we got a wet bench and a long walk.
lines.transcript: No water, no work, no pay. Rilford got its mill. We got a wet bench and a long walk

lines.speaker: quarry_hand
lines.text: We cut. We load. There is a guard at the sluice door and we do not ask why. The village looks at us like we drank the well.
lines.transcript: We cut, we load. There is a guard at the sluice door, and we do not ask why. The village looks at us like we drank the well.

lines.speaker: quarry_hand
lines.text: Night crew. My eyes are a bag of sand. But they pay us, and the board says it is fair, so I say nothing.
lines.transcript: Night crew. My eyes are a bag of sand, but they pay us and the board says it is fair, so I say nothing

lines.speaker: quarry_hand
lines.text: Foreman Kest is gone. Somebody has to sign for the crew. If the reeve and the steward want a witness for the quarry, it is me — I will carry it as well as I can.
lines.transcript: Foreman Kest is gone. Somebody has to sign for the crew. If the Reeve and the steward want a witness for the quarry, it is me. I will carry it as well as I can

lines.speaker: village_baker
lines.text: No water, no dough. If you have not looked at the dry channel behind the mill, do. The reeve is trying, but you cannot ask a bucket to do a river's work.
lines.transcript: No water, no dough. If you have not looked at the dry channel behind the mill, do. The Reeve is trying, but you cannot ask a bucket to do a river's work.

lines.speaker: village_baker
lines.text: Loaves by evening, and I will bake extra for anyone who worked to get the water back. The quarry crew can come to my door and ask; I will not turn them away.
lines.transcript: Loaves by evening, and I will bake extra for anyone who worked to get the water back. The quarry crew can come to my door and ask. I will not turn them away.

lines.speaker: village_baker
lines.text: Half a bucket a day and a long queue at the well. I hope the quarry stone was worth it.
lines.transcript: Half a bucket a day and a long queue at the well. I hope the quarry stone was worth it

lines.speaker: village_baker
lines.text: Bread in the daytime, when the mill turns. Nights the flour sits. It is a strange rhythm, but the board says it is ours.
lines.transcript: Bread in the daytime when the mill turns Nights the flour sits It is a strange rhythm But the board says it is ours

lines.speaker: village_baker
lines.text: Mara is gone. Someone has to mind the noticeboard and speak for the village. I will — I am not the reeve, but I know every household.
lines.transcript: Mara is gone. Someone has to mind the notice board and speak for the village. I will. I am not the Reeve, but I know every household
